description: Anchor-binding experiment, COMPLETE (cycles 2-3, 2026-08-17): the owned A->B chained pairs. Question: does a supplied first-frame anchor pixel-bind B[0]? NO on veo-3.1-fast-prod at 720p or 1080p (cycle 2), and NO on veo-3.1-prod QUALITY at 720p (cycle 3) — identity/wardrobe/set bind, GEOMETRY does not (non-rigid restage on every arm: no global translation within ±16px or uniform scale 0.85-1.15x reduces the mismatch). Pixel-chaining is dead on every door; extend-clip's motion-nulls constraint is DOCTRINE. These mp4s are PAID, NON-REGENERABLE artifacts — do not delete; everything else in the repo's fixture set is rebuildable, this is not.

generation.prompt: Continue the shot from this exact moment with no pause and no reset: he keeps breathing slowly, shoulders rising and falling, the long coat swaying almost imperceptibly as it settles around him; his stare stays locked into the lens, jaw set; the camera keeps its slow, steady drift. Motion continues at the same speed from the very first frame — no freeze, no restart, no new entrance.
generation.prompt_note: MOTION ONLY by design — the anchor carries all appearance; the open question was whether words carry velocity. On fast: no (VR 0.45 / 0.33, restart-stall or slow-run). On quality-720p: YES, near enough — VR 0.64, flat B-head series ~2.05, no restart, kinematic channel PASSES at every trim. Quality fails the OTHER channel (geometric restage).
generation.conditioning: first-frame only (instance.image), durationSeconds 4, generateAudio false, aspectRatio 9:16; identical prompt + anchor on all arms

a_tail.what: frames 144-191 of s4bv5_toss.mp4, re-encoded libx264 CRF 18 so the fixture runs offline forever
a_tail.index_map: full-clip frame N == a_tail frame N-144; the anchor-1 cut point A:190 == a_tail:46
a_tail.reencode_drift: verdicts identical to the full clip; ratios shift by <0.07 (720 arm 2.844 vs canonical 2.775; q720 arm 2.014 vs canonical 1.965)

b_720.head_trim_sweep: NO pass window at any B-start 0-12; ratio RISES with trim (2.8 -> 5.6) because B drifts further from A as it plays
b_720.kinematic_profile: SLOW-RUN, not restart-stall: B-head deltas flat ~1.4 (~0.45x of A's 3.2 tail) with NO ramp in 13 frames — head-trim can never recover a flat series

b_1080.head_trim_sweep: NO pass window; ratio 1.8-3.2 at every trim (the restage's scale pop rides every frame pairing)
b_1080.kinematic_profile: restart-ramp variant: 2.05 -> 0.79 -> ramp to 2.3 by frame 12, never reaching A's 3.2

b_q720_quality.head_trim_sweep: NO pass window; kinematic PASSES at every B-start 0-12 (VR 0.63-0.76) but photometric fails everywhere and RISES monotonically with trim (1.97 -> 5.72) — geometry restaged, so B diverges from A as it plays and no trim exists
b_q720_quality.kinematic_profile: NO restart on quality: B-head deltas FLAT at ~2.05 (0.64x of A's 3.22 tail) from frame 0 — the velocity handoff quality was hoped to fix is in fact fixed; the anchor bind it was hoped to provide is not
b_q720_quality.note: PSNR 25.56 vs fast-720p's 25.52 — statistically the same restage magnitude. The church-grim near-pixel-exact observation (2026-07-20) does not reproduce under instrumentation.

verdicts.conclusion: Pixel-chaining is DEAD on every current door: fast-720p, fast-1080p, quality-720p (and 1080p demotes anchors on both models). The two models fail on OPPOSITE channels — fast carries geometry poorly AND velocity poorly; quality carries velocity (VR 0.64, no restart) but restages geometry identically to fast. A two-channel gate is therefore not optional: a kinematic-only gate ships the quality join, a photometric-only-PSNR gate rewards fast's frozen restarts. DOCTRINE (extend-clip SKILL.md): joins are invisible only at motion nulls — plan cut points at natural pauses or spend a deliberate reframe cut.
